newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli PM rules out multi-year inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Israeli PM rules out multi-year inflation target.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday rejected a Bank of Israel demand for a multi-year inflation target but agreed to set the 1998 goal in the first half of next year, Treasury and central bank sources said.

Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel agreed at a meeting on Tuesday on a goal of achieving "Western" levels of inflation by the year 2001. Israel's inflation will exceed 10 percent this year.
They affirmed Meridor's announcement earlier this week that next year's inflation target would be seven to 10 percent, down from eight to 10 percent this year.
The 1998 target will be fixed in the first half of 1997, before deliberations begin on the 1998 budget, the sources said.
Bank of Israel officials said they were satisfied with the decision, although Bank of Israel sources have said Frenkel wanted a multi-year target to facilitate monetary policy.
